svg.title: 1212 Lobdel Avenue — Fee-Simple Lot Yield Analysis vs PUD Treatment
svg.desc: Four site plan diagrams comparing PUD treatment (current, 4 rows) versus three fee-simple subdivision approaches showing how individual lot setbacks affect yield, culminating in the optimized shared-easement approach yielding 54-60 units in 6 rows.
svg.text: Fee-Simple Lot Subdivision vs PUD — Effect on Yield
36 units · 4 rows · setbacks at site boundary
36 units · 4 rows · each lot needs own front AND rear yard
C — Fee-Simple, Back-to-Back + 15 ft Alley Easement
36 units · 4 rows · alley replaces rear yard (still same yield)
Smaller than PUD or Plan B
54 units · 6 rows · drive aisle counts as rear yard easement
Shared drive easement · 20 ft = rear yard
Shared drive easement · 20 ft = rear yard
Shared drive easement · 20 ft = rear yard
Shared drive easement · 20 ft = rear yard
Shared drive easement · 20 ft = rear yard
Rear yard / boundary · ~20 ft (2.6ft surplus to N line)
Critical flags for fee-simple Approach D:
1. Rear yard easement interpretation must be confirmed with City of Wilmington Land Use — requires pre-application meeting.
2. Each unit needs individual mortgage (standard deed of trust, not PUD rider) — favorable for WHA homeownership program.
3. HOA documents required for shared drive easements, stormwater, and utility infrastructure.
4. 54 units at Scn B modular hard cost: ~$170K/unit — subsidy gap inverts to negative (surplus over $215K target).
5. No amenity zone in Approach D — site nearly fully consumed. Community green must be internal (courtyards) or off-site.
All plans same scale · Parcel 2605130241 · 175 ft × 352.6 ft · 1.39 ac · R-3, Chapter 48 City of Wilmington
